pride_data.title: Folding of beta-tubulin by the chaperonin TRiC/CCT studied by chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the folding of the client protein, beta-tubulin, by the chaperonin TRiC/CCT. Different complexes containing TRiC/CCT and/or the chaperone prefoldin were cross-linked in absence or presence of nucleotides with the homobifunctional, noncleavable reagent, disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS).
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking using DSS was performed following previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014). Samples were digested using endoproteinase Lys-C followed by trypsin. Digests were fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography and SEC fractions were analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos system. Additional experimental details are provided in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequences of target proteins and identified contaminants. Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 20 ppm. The original scoring scheme of xQuest (Rinner et al., Nat. Methods, 2008) was used. False discovery rates (FDRs) were controlled by searches against shuffled sequences of all database entries. The FDR was set to <5% at the non-redundant peptide-pair level. Cross-linking identifications are compiled in a spreadsheet in Microsoft Excel format; a separate spreadsheet connects the raw files and the individual cross-linking experiments.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; protein folding
